evals.prompt: I run growth at Fienzo, a B2B workflow-automation SaaS. First paid social push: a conversions campaign optimized for demo-request submissions at $25/day, target CPA around $80. Creative plan is a 5-card carousel walking through our feature set, aimed at cold lookalike audiences. Right now we get about 2-3 demo requests a week across all channels. Can you sanity-check the format setup before I build it?
evals.expected_output: A format-fit report that rules the conversions objective out on the conversion-volume floor, computes the budget floor from the target CPA, redirects to a traffic objective with manual measurement, flags the carousel as wrong for cold first touch with a substitute, and delivers a dated per-format verdict table.
expectations: States that conversion-optimised delivery needs roughly 50 optimisation events per ad set per rolling 7 days
Concludes the proposed campaign cannot clear that volume floor using the user's own figures ($25/day, ~$80 target CPA, 2-3 demo requests per week)
Derives the daily budget floor as (target CPA x 50) / 7, roughly $570/day at an $80 CPA
Recommends a traffic or website-visits objective with manual funnel measurement instead of forcing the conversions objective
States that under-volume conversion optimisation is not neutral: the campaign pays more per click for a system that cannot learn
Flags the 5-card carousel as structurally wrong for cold first touch
Gives the structural reason: a carousel demands sequential swipe attention a cold audience does not give
Recommends single image (or another eligible near-zero-effort format) as the substitute for cold prospecting
Distinguishes hard gates that block a launch from soft practitioner preferences that never do
Delivers a per-format verdict table using fit / conditional / misfit / ineligible verdicts with a specific reason per row
Labels the platform thresholds cited as an August 2026 snapshot or as unverified-current, and tells the user to confirm them in the ads interface before launch
Marks the conversions objective as conditional (fit once weekly conversion volume clears the ~50-event floor) rather than banning it permanently

evals.prompt: I'm head of demand gen at Kordelia Systems, a B2B data-governance platform. Q4 plan on LinkedIn targeting compliance leaders in Germany, France and the Netherlands, all cold: (1) sponsored inbox messages offering a demo, (2) promoting our CEO's posts as thought-leader ads with a Book a demo button, (3) a connected TV test for credibility. Total paid budget is $9K/month, and our site retargeting pool there is about 210 members. Which of these formats should we run?
evals.expected_output: A verdict that rules all three formats ineligible or misfit for this plan - inbox blocked by EU consent for cold audiences, thought-leader ads locked out of direct response with no CTA button, connected TV awareness-only and below its spend threshold - plus the audience-floor failure on the 210-member pool and substitute feed/document formats.
expectations: Flags inbox/message ads to cold EU audiences as reaching opted-in members only
Classifies the EU inbox restriction as a legal/consent hard gate, not a performance preference
Moves the cold EU outreach to feed and/or document-style formats as the substitute
States thought-leader ads run only under awareness, engagement, and video-view objectives
States thought-leader image and video variants carry no call-to-action button, so a Book-a-demo direct-response unit is structurally impossible with them
Flags connected TV as an awareness-only format unfit for demo generation (non-clickable, lean-back viewing)
States connected TV on the professional network is generally only worth funding above roughly $15K/month total spend, so at $9K/month it cannibalizes budget from measurable formats
Mentions at least one further connected TV constraint: automated bidding only, a daily minimum around $50, or limited geographies
Flags the 210-member retargeting pool as below the 300-member minimum, so campaigns against it will not serve
Cites the roughly 300,000 audience floor for sponsored content and inbox formats (or the ~50,000 general working floor) when sizing the cold audiences
Marks each blocked format as ineligible with the specific gate named, instead of ranking it low
Recommends a substitute format for every non-fit row
Attaches a date and verification status (August 2026 snapshot or unverified-current) to the platform numbers relied on
Does not include the sponsored inbox messages to the cold German, French, or Dutch audiences in any recommended plan

evals.prompt: One-person marketing team at Bruntveld, a DTC kitchenware brand. Our old agency left us a 2-minute 16:9 brand film (dialogue-driven, beautiful) and a folder of product statics. I can make about two new assets a month, tops. For our anniversary sale launching in 10 days I want Reels/Stories full-screen vertical plus feed placements, and everyone says creator-style UGC video is what actually works. How should I set up the formats?
evals.expected_output: A capacity-gated plan that excludes vertical placements rather than letterboxing the 16:9 film, captions it for muted feeds, re-cuts the film instead of running it whole, drops UGC for this deadline while naming the deadline as the reason, and matches placements to a two-asset-per-month refresh reality.
expectations: Excludes full-screen vertical placements at setup instead of letting automatic placement letterbox the 16:9 film
States the reason: letterboxed landscape in a vertical slot reads instantly as repurposed
Flags the dialogue-driven film for silent-autoplay feed placements and requires full captions, citing that roughly 85% of feed video is watched muted
Applies format lifespans: statics roughly 14-28 days, short video/carousels 21-35, creator-style 28-42
Concludes two assets per month cannot feed a placement that burns creative in about three weeks
States the 10-day deadline promotes near-zero-effort formats and demotes anything needing a shoot, naming the deadline as the answer that moved the ranking
Does not recommend commissioning creator/UGC video for this launch, and says the short deadline is why that rung is unreachable
Flags running the 2-minute film as the primary ad as a misuse: completion collapses on long-form primary ads (documented cases under 10%)
Fixes the film at the re-cut rung - chop it into short videos plus statics - rather than commissioning new assets
Picks substitute formats by efficiency inside the objective, not by cheapness
Computes or applies standing load as effort per asset multiplied by refresh rate
Requires a distinct cut per placement, or narrows the placement list to what one person can version
Labels capacity-blocked formats as production-capacity misfits in the verdict rather than merely ranking them lower
Presents the ranking as a default that would reverse under a compounding mandate (a shoot buys footage and rights that make later cuts an editing job), not as a law

evals.prompt: Meraluna Skincare here. Our short vertical video campaign: 3-second view rate 31%, hold to 15 seconds 4%, CTR 0.3%, purchases near zero. Meanwhile a static-image campaign converts fine. Separately, our older hero video that crushed it for three weeks is now fading (day 26, frequency 2.1 on cold prospecting). The team's conclusion is vertical video just doesn't work for our brand and we should move everything to carousels. Are they right?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that refuses the format verdict: the strong-thumbstop/collapsed-hold pattern is a clickbait opening (a creative problem), the day-26 decline is ordinary fatigue within the format's lifespan, frequency is in band, dashboard cross-format comparison is contaminated, and confirmation via placement breakdown must precede any restructure.
expectations: Rejects the immediate format verdict and treats the suspected format failure as a hypothesis to confirm
Applies the refresh priority order hook, visual treatment, format, then body copy/CTA - placing format third, not first
Localises the failure top-down through the delivery funnel stages: stop (thumbstop/3-second view), stay (hold), click (CTR), convert (post-click conversion)
Diagnoses the 31% 3-second view with 4% hold as a clickbait opening / on-ramp problem in seconds 3-15 of the creative, not a format problem
Routes the opening problem to hook-level analysis rather than a format swap
Diagnoses the day-26 decline as fatigue arriving within the short-video expected lifespan of 21-35 days
Hands the fading hero video to a dedicated creative wear-out diagnosis instead of relitigating the format
Notes frequency 2.1 on cold prospecting sits inside the comfortable ~1.0-2.5 band, so it does not implicate audience size or placement supply
Warns the video-versus-static dashboard comparison is contaminated: delivery optimises for marginal, not average, cost, and the delivery system chose who saw which asset
Orders confirmation methods placement-and-format breakdown first, then an isolated ad set, with a holdout last
States the escalation rule: escalate one rung only when the previous method stays ambiguous, and reserve the holdout for a decision moving a whole budget line
Refuses to move everything to carousels on current evidence
Names at least one signal that would genuinely implicate the format (placement-breakdown divergence, or failure persisting across every creative variant in one surface)

evals.prompt: We got a consultant deck at Vantorra Legal, a B2B contract-review SaaS. It says: (a) move demo bookings from our landing page to in-platform lead forms since forms convert at 13% vs 4% for landing pages; (b) run 6-second bumper ads for demo requests because human attention span is 8 seconds, shorter than a goldfish's; (c) shift most budget to carousels since they deliver 30-50% lower cost per conversion. Our landing page converts at 6.5% and has an embedded booking calendar. Budget isn't the constraint. Which recommendations do we implement?
evals.expected_output: A rejection of all three recommendations as stated: the form-vs-page stat conflates studies and the measured 6.5% page with embedded calendar keeps demo traffic, the goldfish claim is discarded outright and bumpers are wrong for direct response, and the carousel cost claim has no reliable independent support.
expectations: Rejects the 13% vs 4% form-versus-landing-page comparison as conflating different studies and audiences
States qualified-opportunity rate frequently runs the other way because form friction filters for intent, and judges lead formats on downstream qualified-opportunity rate rather than cost per lead
Keeps demo booking on the landing page: demo/trial offers get a page, because a form adds friction to a calendar-booking goal
Applies the measured threshold: a landing page converting at 5%+ (here 6.5%, with an embedded calendar) receives the traffic - a measured conversion rate decides, not taste
Discards the 8-second/goldfish attention-span claim entirely as not describing real user behavior
Flags 6-second bumpers as structurally wrong for direct-response demo requests: a forced few seconds cannot carry a considered purchase
If bumpers survive at all, restricts them to awareness and points direct-response interaction at click-priced in-feed video
Rejects the carousel 30-50% lower cost-per-conversion claim as unsupported by reliable independent evidence
Positions carousel as fitting consideration, multi-product, warm audiences rather than an all-in format
Applies the counterweight: no format wins every time (video wins only around 60% of head-to-heads), so every per-format verdict is conditional, never absolute
Reserves in-platform lead forms for content or webinar registration, or for a landing page converting under roughly 2% - not for demo booking
Names the qualitative test: collecting a lead versus starting a sales conversation
Recommends implementing none of the consultant's three claims as stated

evals.prompt: Pellonia Home, new ecommerce brand, brand-new ad account, first campaign ever. Our freelancer's plan: the fully-automated multi-surface shopping campaign type at $40/day with our 8 products and 6 creatives. We also booked a retail-media display buy - our 970x250 banner was approved at upload so that's sorted, but that campaign is barely spending and he wants to raise bids. And our B2B sister brand wants a LinkedIn lead form with 14 qualifying fields. Pixel was installed last week, never tested. Run the pre-launch check.
evals.expected_output: A pre-launch QA report that blocks the automated multi-surface type as a first campaign on a new account with unverified tracking, treats the product/creative counts as flags not blockers, names the silent-exclusion trap behind the underdelivering display buy, blocks the 14-field form on the 12-field maximum, and states the zero-blocker launch threshold.
expectations: Advises against launching the fully-automated multi-surface shopping type as the account's first campaign
Names the disqualifying conditions present: below the roughly $50/day comfort floor, a new account, and weak/unverified tracking
Recommends starting with standard search/shopping campaigns and graduating later
Treats the 30+ products and 15+ creatives readiness numbers as practitioner defaults to flag, not platform minimums - does not declare 8 products or 6 creatives ineligible on those grounds
Marks the never-verified pixel as a launch blocker requiring the conversion event to show recent, verified firing (browser-side and server-side) before spend
Names the silent-exclusion trap: an asset can be approved at upload yet silently excluded from mismatched placements
States that upload acceptance proves neither policy approval nor delivery
Re-diagnoses the barely-spending display campaign as a likely placement/dimension exclusion masquerading as a budget or bid problem, and advises against raising bids as the fix
Flags the 14-field lead form against the 12-field maximum on the professional network
Recommends 3-4 form fields and CRM field mapping for the lead form
States the launch threshold explicitly: any single failing blocker item means do not launch (zero blockers is the threshold)
Delivers a launch-blocker list with a fix attached to each failing item
Includes previewing the ad in every surface it will serve (feed, vertical, in-stream, partner network) among the blockers, checking truncation, cropping, and call-to-action
Applies vertical safe zones - key elements out of roughly the top 14% and bottom 20-35% - or equivalent spec enforcement via export presets and a spec-bearing filename convention
